name: Copper Clad Laminates & PCB Base Materials
scope: The AI-server-driven global squeeze in CCL, glass cloth and copper foil, and India's first ECMS-backed laminate plants at Ratnaveer, Kaynes, Syrma and Amber (Wipro's plant is unlisted).

summary.one_line: New this week: a Choice Institutional Equities plant visit (6 Oct) says Ratnaveer's CCL Line 1 is on track for commissioning in November. Realisation is now about Rs 5,500 per sheet, against the Rs 1,260 assumed at feasibility. Global hikes kept spreading in September (Panasonic +30%, China Jushi glass cloth +15-20%). With the stock up ~109% in a year, much of the story is already priced in.
key_points: Global tightness widened in September. Citi data puts mainstream electronic glass cloth up 118-165% this year; China Jushi raised thick cloth 15% and thin cloth 20% in September. Kingboard's seventh hike of the year takes cumulative FR-4 CCL increases above 100%, and Panasonic raised ordinary multilayer CCL 30% from September (S22). Nan Ya's +20% took effect on 1 Sep (S17).

The structural view is getting bigger. Morgan Stanley sees the CCL market growing from US$19bn in 2025 to US$47bn by 2030, and expects a 31% HVLP4 copper-foil shortfall in 2027 and a 20% gap in 2028 (S22). In July, Goldman Sachs expected a second round of M7-and-above CCL hikes of 10-15% QoQ around end-Q3/start-Q4 2026 (S23).

India still imports more than 90% of its CCL, per Ratnaveer, in a domestic market sized at over Rs 5,000 cr (S7). Ind-Ra says the imports come mainly from China (S20). PIB states that laminate is about 30% of PCB bill-of-materials cost (S25). ECMS gives laminate, copper foil and prepreg a 25% capex incentive (S3). Cumulative approvals reached Rs 69,548 cr after the 17 Aug tranche (S15), and we found no new tranche up to 14 Oct.

Ratnaveer, new from Choice's 6 Oct visit: Line 1 machinery has been dispatched from China and commissioning next month is on track. The building can house 5 lines, and additional lines will be added at roughly 6-month intervals once Line 1 stabilises. The project gets a 50% capex subsidy (25% central plus 25% state) (S21). Order booking is still due from 31 Oct and trial production in the second week of Dec (S6).

Ratnaveer's CCL economics have changed sharply. Realisation is now about Rs 5,500 per sheet against Rs 1,260 assumed at feasibility, so management says a single line could generate about Rs 600 cr of revenue (S21). Sources differ on timing for the Rs 750 cr CCL revenue target: FY29 per Choice (S21), FY31 per ICICI Direct's July note (S7).

Syrma's CCL comes through a 51:49 JV with Korea's Shinhyup Electronics: a Rs 1,595 cr plant at Naidupeta (Andhra Pradesh) with Rs 856 cr of state incentives, targeted in 2025 for commissioning by Oct 2026 (S24). ICICI Direct's May 2026 note models PCB revenue only from FY28, and we found no commissioning announcement (S11).

Valuations on 13 Oct 2026: Ratnaveer trades at 43.5x P/E, 7.8% below its 52-week high, and is up ~109% over one year (S8, S21). Syrma is at 83.3x and 4.7% off its high (S10). Kaynes is at 62.6x and 54.9% off its high (S9).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Ratnaveer: its first line starts in a market where CCL realisation is roughly 4x the feasibility assumption (S21). It also gets a 50% capex subsidy, and its buyers get a 2% cashback for purchasing locally (S21).
Indian PCB makers would gain a local laminate source. Ratnaveer names Fine-Line and CG Power among its target clients (S21). Kaynes, Syrma and Amber plan captive CCL (S4, S19, S24).

Upstream suppliers could gain a new local customer. Ratnaveer expects to source copper foil domestically from players like Hindalco in future, and buys epoxy partly in India (S21). Atul makes epoxy for electrical and electronics uses (S12).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: PCB and EMS makers that buy imported laminate. At Amber, CCL inflation has cut the PCB margin to about 12% from a normal 16% (S19). Supplier hikes kept coming in September (S22).

Indian CCL lines will import glass fabric and copper foil at first (S21), and those are the inputs driving the cost spike (S18, S22). Ratnaveer's technology rests on Chinese technical staff hired on 3-year contracts (S21).

Ratnaveer has re-rated ahead of first output. The stock is at Rs 332 versus the Rs 264 rights price (S8, S5), and its promoter holding fell to 38.71% in Sep-26 from 45.49% in Jun-26 (S21). Customers have not signed contracts yet (S6).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Ratnaveer: order bookings from 31 Oct, commissioning in November and trial production in the second week of Dec 2026. Watch also for upward revisions to guidance once production stabilises (S6, S21).
Syrma: any confirmation that the Shinhyup JV plant has been commissioned (target was Oct 2026) (S24). Kaynes: PCB commercialisation from Q3 FY27 (S13).
Whether high-end CCL hikes land at the 10-15% QoQ Goldman expected (S23), and whether glass cloth reaches the $1.75-2.19/m forecast for Q4 2026 (S1).

sections.title: What CCL is and why it is tight

subsections.title: CCL and prepreg in the PCB value chain

blocks.text: A copper clad laminate (CCL) is the base sheet of a PCB. It is woven glass cloth impregnated with resin (usually epoxy) and clad with copper foil. Prepreg is the resin-impregnated glass layer that bonds the layers of a multi-layer board (S4). PIB puts laminate at about 30% of a PCB's bill-of-materials cost (S25). Suppliers name glass cloth and copper foil as the main drivers of their 2026 hikes (S18, S22).

AI servers need low-loss laminates (M7 class and above), thin low-Dk glass and HVLP copper foil. AtlasPCB says these are allocation-only (S2), and Goldman Sachs names HVLP4 foil and Low-Dk 2 glass as the cost drivers for high-end CCL (S23).

subsections.title: 2026 shortage: prices, lead times, new capacity

blocks.text: New supply takes time. Glass weaving looms have 18-24 month lead times, and AtlasPCB expects new glass cloth capacity from mid-to-late 2027 (S1). Doosan's Thailand CCL plant targets mass production in H2 2028 (S16). Morgan Stanley raised its 2030 CCL market estimate to US$47bn from US$35-40bn earlier. It calls this a specification-driven structural cycle (S22).

The price data comes from trade press (AtlasPCB, SMM, 36Kr), broker notes reported in the press, and supplier notices. None of it is an audited index, and realised prices may differ from list-price hikes.

sections.title: Import dependence, ECMS and Indian laminate capex

blocks.text: Ratnaveer puts India's CCL import share at over 90% of a domestic market worth more than Rs 5,000 cr (company estimate, S7). Ind-Ra notes the imports come mainly from China. A 30% anti-dumping duty on bare PCBs has lifted domestic PCB plant utilisation to 70-90%, but without local CCL, value addition stays limited (S20). PIB lists laminate approvals for Syrma Components and Ratnaveer under ECMS (S25).

blocks.caption: ECMS incentive structure for PCB and laminate segments

blocks.text: Source: India Briefing summary of ECMS guidelines (S3). Gujarat matches the central capex support, so Ratnaveer is eligible for a 50% capex subsidy overall, paid out as the plant operates (S21). Cumulative ECMS approvals stand at Rs 69,548 cr across 106 applications, above the Rs 59,350 cr investment target. The 17 Aug tranche added Rs 1,033 cr to Wipro's laminate project (S15).

subsections.title: Ratnaveer: a steel company adding a laminate business

blocks.text: Ratnaveer makes stainless steel finishing sheets, washers, fasteners and tubes and pipes. It reported FY26 revenue of Rs 1,069 cr at a 10.5% EBITDA margin (S21). Management guides FY27 revenue of Rs 1,350-1,400 cr (+26-31%). For FY29 it targets Rs 2,500 cr in total: Rs 1,800 cr from steel and Rs 750 cr from CCL, at a blended EBITDA margin of about 14% versus 10.5% in FY26 (S21). Choice describes this guidance as conservative until CCL production stabilises (S21).

blocks.caption: Ratnaveer CCL plan: what changed this week
rows: Rs 750 cr in FY29 at ~20% EBITDA, ~13% PAT
Rs 750+ cr by FY31, Rs 150 cr EBITDA (ICICI Direct, 27 Jul) (S7)
Built for 5 lines; initial capex ~Rs 400 cr; on promoter-leased land
Machinery dispatched from China; commissioning next month on track

blocks.text: Source for the Choice column: S21. Glass fabric and copper foil will be imported at first. Epoxy will come from India and China. The company hopes to source copper foil domestically, for example from Hindalco, in future. Technical know-how comes from Chinese personnel on 3-year contracts, and the CCL business is led by an executive with 28+ years in CCL (S21).

The jump to ~Rs 5,500 per sheet reflects 2026 spot conditions (S21, S22). If prices revert when new global capacity arrives in 2027-28 (S1, S16), the one-line revenue math would shrink accordingly. Choice's capex figure is printed as 'INR 4,0000 Mn' in the note; we read it as ~Rs 400 cr.

blocks.text: Amber's PCB margin fell to about 12% from a normal 16% because of CCL price rises. Recovery from Q3 FY27 assumed no further CCL increases (S19), but Panasonic, Nan Ya and Kingboard all raised prices again from late August (S17, S22). At Kaynes, ICICI Direct records component prices up 30-35% and lead times of 6-8 months (S13).

subsections.title: Can Indian plants make AI-server grades?

blocks.text: No Indian company has disclosed qualification for M7-class or other ultra-low-loss grades. The AI-server tightness is concentrated in these grades, and their cost drivers are HVLP4 foil and Low-Dk glass (S23, S2). Ratnaveer's named target clients are domestic PCB makers, and management cites PCB, EV, defence and semiconductor demand rather than AI servers (S7, S21). Syrma's plant draws on Korean partner Shinhyup for technology and marketing (S24).

Our reading: the first Indian lines will most likely make standard FR-4 for domestic consumer, auto and industrial PCBs, using imported glass fabric and copper foil (S21). Ram Ratna Wires' 2023 plan for PCB laminates and copper foil has had no follow-up disclosure that we could find (S26).

subsections.title: Broker coverage of the laminate angle

items: Choice Institutional Equities (6 Oct 2026, management meet and plant visit, not rated) is new this week. It sets its sector view to Positive and calls Ratnaveer at an inflection point. It lists on-time Line 1 commissioning, PCB customer approvals and working capital during the ramp-up as the key monitorables (S21).
ICICI Direct (27 Jul 2026) on Ratnaveer leaves CCL out of its FY27-28 estimates until execution is clearer (S7).
ICICI Direct (17 Aug 2026) on Amber quantifies the CCL cost hit to an Indian PCB maker: a PCB margin of about 12% against a normal 16% (S19).

Global brokers, reported in the press: Morgan Stanley sees the CCL market at US$47bn by 2030 and an HVLP4 copper-foil shortfall (S22). Goldman Sachs expects a second round of high-end CCL price hikes (S23).
Ind-Ra (Jun 2025) treats local CCL as the missing link for PCB value addition (S20).

blocks.caption: Screener.in snapshot with reference points
rows: Rs 339 on 6 Oct (Choice); Rs 197 on 27 Jul (ICICI Direct); Rs 264 rights price; 1Y +109.4%

blocks.text: Sources: S8, S9, S10, S21, S7, S13, S5, S19. Ratnaveer has roughly doubled in a year, against +16% for BSE Metals (S21), although broker estimates published so far exclude CCL (S7). Kaynes' de-rating stems from working-capital concerns rather than laminates (S13). Syrma trades near its high at 83.3x P/E, before any laminate revenue (S10, S11).

items: Commissioning slippage: Syrma's JV was reported in 2025 as commissioning by Oct 2026 (S24), but ICICI Direct models PCB revenue from FY28 (S11). Ratnaveer moved its start from 'commercial production November' (S7) to trial production in December (S6), although Choice reports commissioning next month as on track (S21).

Imported inputs: glass fabric and copper foil will be imported at first (S21), and those are exactly the inputs driving global CCL hikes (S22). Morgan Stanley expects HVLP4 foil to stay short through 2028 (S22).
Price cycle: per-sheet realisation is about 4x feasibility assumptions (S21). New global capacity in 2027-28 (S1, S16) could push prices down while Indian lines are still ramping up.
Customer qualification and technology: no Ratnaveer contracts are signed yet (S6), and its process know-how relies on Chinese personnel on fixed-term contracts (S21).

Funding and ownership: Ratnaveer raised Rs 329.99 cr in its rights issue (S5). Its debt is expected to rise to Rs 475 cr by FY28E (S7), and its promoter holding fell to 38.71% in Sep-26 (S21). Amber's net debt rose to about Rs 1,225 cr by Jun 2026 (S19).

companies.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
companies.role: Stainless steel products maker building an ECMS- and Gujarat-approved CCL plant in Vadodara, sized for 5 lines (S7, S21).
companies.impact: Line 1 commissioning is on track for November. Realisation is about Rs 5,500 per sheet, and the CCL target is Rs 750 cr revenue at ~20% EBITDA by FY29 per Choice, or FY31 per ICICI Direct (S21, S7). The stock is up ~109% in a year and trades at 43.5x P/E (S21, S8).

companies.name: Kaynes Technology India Ltd
companies.role: EMS company whose subsidiary Kaynes Circuits holds an INR 32.8b ECMS approval for multi-layer and HDI PCBs, camera modules and CCL (S4).
companies.impact: PCB and OSAT commercialisation is due from Q3 FY27 (S13). CCL mainly lowers its own PCB costs. The stock is 54.9% below its 52-week high on working-capital concerns (S9, S13).

companies.name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
companies.role: EMS company building PCB, HDI/flex and CCL capacity through a 51:49 JV with Korea's Shinhyup Electronics at Naidupeta: a Rs 1,595 cr plant with Rs 856 cr of AP incentives (S24, S25).
companies.impact: The JV targeted commissioning by Oct 2026 (S24), but ICICI Direct sees PCB revenue only from FY28 (S11). The stock trades at 83.3x P/E, near its 52-week high (S10).

companies.name: Amber Enterprises India Ltd
companies.role: AC and EMS maker investing about Rs 4,300 cr in bare PCBs under ECMS, with its first CCL plant planned by FY29-30 (S19).
companies.impact: Its PCB margin fell to about 12% from 16% on CCL inflation. The recovery assumed no further hikes (S19), but more hikes came in September (S22).

companies.name: Fine-Line Circuits Ltd
companies.role: Microcap PCB maker. Ratnaveer names 'Fine Line' among the PCB makers it is targeting as CCL customers (S21).
companies.impact: As a laminate buyer, it faces imported CCL inflation (S22) and could benefit from local supply and the 2% local-purchase cashback (S21).

companies.name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd
companies.role: Named by Ratnaveer management as a target CCL customer (S21).
companies.impact: Adjacent customer only. Laminate would be a small input for it, with no disclosed CCL supply agreement (S21).

companies.name: Hindalco Industries Ltd
companies.role: Named by Ratnaveer as a prospective future domestic supplier of copper foil for CCL (S21).
companies.impact: Adjacent large cap. We found no PCB-grade copper foil disclosure from Hindalco, so treat this as an option.

companies.name: Ram Ratna Wires Ltd
companies.role: Copper winding wire maker. In Mar 2023 its board approved a Bhiwadi facility for PCBs, PCB laminates and copper foil, at Rs 200 cr over five years (S26).
companies.impact: A stated laminate and copper-foil ambition with no further disclosure that we found. Treat it as an option, not a project.

companies.name: Atul Ltd
companies.role: Makes Lapox epoxy resins and curing agents for markets including electrical and electronics (S12).
companies.impact: Ratnaveer sources epoxy partly in India (S21), so Atul is a potential local resin supplier. It has not disclosed CCL-specific supply.

method: Weekly refresh of the 2026-W41 edition, researched on 14 Oct 2026 with web search and page fetches. Market data comes from screener.in as of 13 Oct 2026 (numbers.json). New this week: Choice Institutional Equities' 6 Oct 2026 Ratnaveer plant-visit note, read from the PDF (realisation per sheet, FY29 targets, 5-line facility, 50% subsidy, raw-material sourcing, target clients, shareholding). Also new: 36Kr's 15 Sep report of Morgan Stanley and Citi data plus September price hikes at Panasonic, China Jushi and Kingboard; Goldman Sachs' high-end CCL view via UDN; Outlook Business on the Syrma-Shinhyup JV; and a PIB release on laminate approvals and laminate's share of PCB cost. The PIB page returned 403, so it is cited from search-result text, and its date is inferred from Ratnaveer's 30 Mar 2026 ECMS approval date. The ECMS cumulative figure was re-verified on the Tribune/ANI page, replacing Multibagg. Dropped: the Investing.com Kaynes transcript, Angel One's Wipro 100%-import claim and Wipro capacity details (we now show >90% per Ratnaveer only), Trade Brains, Cyient DLM (no laminate link), and Fine-Line's screener page. Added: CG Power and Hindalco as adjacent names cited by Ratnaveer management. We found no new ECMS tranche, no Kaynes/Syrma plant start-up announcement and no new CCL supplier notice dated October 2026. The sources disagree on the year Ratnaveer reaches Rs 750 cr of CCL revenue (FY29 per Choice, FY31 per ICICI Direct), so both are shown. Grasim was dropped because its only source was a 2021 capacity article with no CCL link. Coverage spans large cap (Hindalco, CG Power), mid cap (Kaynes, Syrma, Amber, Atul), small cap (Ratnaveer, Ram Ratna) and microcap (Fine-Line). Ratnaveer remains the only listed standalone laminate maker near commissioning. No ratings or price targets are given.
